transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Lately I feel this heavy, empty mood all the time, like I’m weighed down and can’t shake it no matter what I do. It just feels like I'm carrying this constant darkness around, and I don't know how to make it stop.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty mood?

It’s been going on for a little over a year now, pretty much every single day. It really started not long after I changed my work schedule and picked up all those extra night shifts at the hospital. I just haven't been able to shake it since then.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling this down or depressed at any other time in your life before this past year?

No, I’ve never felt anything like this before in my life. It only started about a year and a half ago, shortly after I began taking on those extra night shifts at work. Before that, I was actually doing really well.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Yes, completely. I used to love painting murals and playing soccer on the weekends, but now I just don't care about any of it anymore. Even when my friends bring by sketches or try to invite me out, I just tell them no because I can't feel any excitement at all.
Since your schedule changed, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your daily energy levels?

My sleep has been completely messed up and irregular ever since I started those late-night shifts. My energy is totally gone, and most days I feel like I'm moving in slow motion, like I'm dragging a hundred-pound backpack just to get around.
During this past year, have you also been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or blaming yourself excessively for things?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling worthless or blaming myself for things. It's more that I just feel completely empty and heavy all the time, like there's just nothing inside.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus on your work, or make everyday decisions lately?

Yes, my head feels incredibly foggy lately and I often lose track of what I'm doing mid-sentence. Even basic things like filling out my chart notes at work or deciding what to cook completely overwhelm me. I often just end up staring blankly at the computer screen or the fridge, unable to make a choice.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or felt like life is not worth living, during this past year?

Yes, pretty often, especially after a long night shift when the emptiness hits hardest, I think it'd be easier if I didn't wake up or if I stepped in front of a train on my way home. I've even looked up which bridge is the highest in the city, though I haven't actually gone there or tried to do anything.
Before this heavy mood started a year and a half ago, did you ever experience milder, ongoing periods of feeling down or low energy that lasted for several years?

No, I don't recall ever having any long-term periods of feeling down or low on energy before this all started a year and a half ago. My mood and energy were generally fine before I took on those extra work shifts.
Have you ever had a period of a few days or more where you felt the exact opposite of this—extremely energetic, hyperactive, or like you didn't need much sleep?
No, I’ve never had any periods where I felt extremely energetic or hyperactive like that. I have also never experienced times where I felt like I didn't need any sleep.
During this difficult time, have you heard voices or seen things that others couldn't, or held any strong beliefs that others told you weren't real?

I haven't heard any voices, but I do have a strong belief that everyone else tells me is not true. I'm convinced the cameras on the hospital unit and even the mirrors at my house are watching me specifically as part of an experiment on my mind. No matter how many times people tell me it's not real, I can't shake the feeling that they are tracking my thoughts.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode lasting over a year, characterized by persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, severe fatigue, sleep disruption, diminished concentration/indecisiveness, and active suicidal ideation (looking up bridges). Additionally, the patient reports delusions of reference and persecution (believing they are being watched and their thoughts tracked via cameras and mirrors as part of an experiment), which meet the criteria for psychotic features during a depressive episode.
